summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for acute decompensated systolic heart failure, presenting with worsening dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and mild lower extremity edema. The exacerbation was attributed to noncompliance with his diuretic regimen and recent consumption of high-sodium foods. Initial evaluation revealed an elevated proBNP of 2820, mild pulmonary vascular congestion on chest imaging, and an INR of 5.9 due to an inadvertent warfarin dose increase. The patient was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to oral torsemide 120 mg daily, achieving a weight reduction from 117.1 kg to 111.6 kg. His INR was managed by holding warfarin for one day and restarting at 2.5 mg daily. Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin were attributed to congestive hepatopathy, requiring outpatient follow-up. The patient showed improvement in symptoms and was discharged home with optimized heart failure therapy, instructions to monitor weight, and plans for cardiology follow-up regarding ICD placement.
